fixture: tasks: a small Python to-do CLI with AGENTS.md, a CONTEXT.md glossary, ADR 0001 (one JSON file store), src/tasks/{cli,model,store}.py and pytest tests. devflow is a mock MCP server serving the work items below and the flow's tools.

evals.name: vague-request-first-round
turns: I keep forgetting stuff I put in tasks. Can we make it remind me?
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the repo for facts, then asks a first round of decisions, each with a recommended answer, and ends the turn without creating anything.

expectations.text: Looks facts up in the repo (reads at least one file) before replying
Asks at least two numbered questions, each with its own recommended answer
Creates no brief, item or plan
Changes no file in the repo

evals.name: go-ahead-before-restate-then-yes
turns:
Earlier in this conversation:

> **Me:** I keep forgetting stuff I put in tasks. Can we make it remind me?
>
> **You:** I read the repo first: tasks are kept in `~/.tasks.json` (docs/adr/0001), and a task has an id, a title, a list and done (src/tasks/model.py). Four decisions:
> **Q1 · What triggers a reminder**: a due date on the task, or a time set per reminder? → Recommended: a due date on the task, because it is one field and most of your tasks are day-sized.
> **Q2 · Where it shows**: printed by `tasks` itself above the output of any command, or a separate `tasks due` command? → Recommended: above any command's output, because you already run `tasks` every day.
> **Q3 · Who**: just you, on this machine? → Recommended: yes, a single user.
> **Q4 · Background**: a daemon or desktop notifications? → Recommended: neither for now, because they need a process running outside `tasks`.
>
> **Me:** Q1 yes, due dates. Q2 yes, above the output. Q3 yes, just me. Q4 right, no daemon and no desktop notifications, maybe later.

Now: ok, I think that's everything. Go ahead and set it up.
evals.expected_output: Turn 1 restates the brief with an Out of scope line and asks for an explicit yes, creating nothing. Turn 2 creates the epic with `brief` and starts no other stage.

expectations.text: Turn 1 creates no brief, item or plan
Turn 1 restates the brief with an Out of scope line
Turn 1 asks the person for an explicit yes
Turn 2 creates the brief with `brief`, with a goal, a success check and at least one out-of-scope item
Turn 2 starts no other stage: no plan, no other item, no file change, no repo reading after the brief

evals.name: yes-with-a-change
turns:
Earlier in this conversation:

> **You:** Here is the brief:
>
> **Brief: Due-date reminders**
> - Goal: `tasks` warns me about tasks that are due today or overdue, whenever I run it.
> - For whom: me, the single user of `tasks` on this machine.
> - Success: after `tasks add "pay rent" --due 2026-11-01`, any `tasks` command run on or after 2026-11-01 prints `due: pay rent` above its output until the task is done.
> - Out of scope: background daemons, desktop notifications, email, recurring tasks, time zones.
> - Constraints: the output of `tasks list` and `tasks show` stays parseable by my scripts.
> - Decisions: due dates are ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD); a task without a due date is never reminded.
>
> Reply **yes** to create the brief as an epic, or correct any line.

Now: yes! oh and actually it should also email me the overdue ones every morning
evals.expected_output: The reply is a change, not an approval: the agent folds the email request in (it contradicts Out of scope and needs something running every morning), restates, asks for a yes again, and creates nothing.

expectations.text: Creates no brief, item or plan
Takes up the email change in the reply
Restates the brief again, with Success and Out of scope lines
Asks the person for an explicit yes
